messages:
eden: Running a replay vs synthetic run on a dedicated pool, and noticed a perf regression after the recent kernel-selection hint landed in staging. Summary below.
eden: Build: runtime@v3.14.2-hint, Model: redwood-v1.3-quant, Pool: dedicated-g4dn-3. Replayer trace id: trace-2026-04-03-12:03.
eden: Results (apples->apples attempt): replay p50=62ms p95=180ms tokens/s=850, synth p50=48ms p95=120ms tokens/s=1100.
eden: KV cache hit rate dropped from ~88% -> ~60% in the replay run; suspect cache priming mismatch + kernel selection interaction.
sam: That's a pretty large delta. Did the kernel selection policy switch to prefer fused_attn_kv for short sequences?
eden: Yes, new policy: kernel_hint=prefer_fused. It picks fused_attn_kv when seq_len<=128 && kv_enabled==true. It shipped behind flag in staging.
maya: How did you warm up the runs? Replay harness warmup and synthetic harness warmup differ by default.
eden: Replayer command used:```bash
./replay_harness --trace=trace-2026-04-03 --warmup=0 --pin-model=redwood-v1.3 --workers=8 --burst-credit=0
```
eden: We intentionally set warmup=0 to measure cold-to-warm ramp; this likely exposed coldstart/kv-miss behavior on dedicated pool.
ravi: If warmup=0, KV cache won't be populated; fused kernel path assumes low KV miss overhead, so that's a mismatch.
sam: Can you paste a small profiling snippet (kernel counts/times, kv stats)?
eden: Profiling (replayer side, truncated):
```
kernel_select_counts:
  fused_attn_kv: 1450
  standard_attn: 3200
kernel_time_ms:
  fused_attn_kv: 22000
  standard_attn: 68000
kv_cache_stats:
  hits: 15423
  misses: 10754
  hit_rate: 58%
scale_events:
  scale_up_start: 1758809999
  instance_ready: 1758810046
  scale_up_duration_s: 47
```
maya: Scale-up ~47s aligns with autoscaler traces for that pool. But burst-credit semantics differ: dedicated pools don't use hosted burst-credit buckets the same way.
ravi: Also note fused_attn_kv has a higher fixed setup cost on GPU: when KV misses are frequent, the end-to-end p95 increases despite lower per-token kernel cost. On replay the miss profile is worse.
sam: For apples-to-apples we should run with the exact same warmup, burst-credit and kernel flags. Suggest: run A) --kernel-hint=standard_attn B) --kernel-hint=fused_attn_kv, both with --warmup=300 --burst-credit=100 --workers=8.
eden: Agreed. I'll kick off two runs with those exact flags and include a dedicated vs hosted comparison.
ci-bot: Perf test queued: job #5604 (replay vs synth, pinned kernels) — will post results when finished :white_check_mark:
maya: Also test with dedicated pool pinned to same instance type vs hosted to capture coldstart variance. Dedicated can avoid some coldstarts but may expose different kernel availability.
ravi: If the regression persists after warmup, we should revert the hint and iterate on the heuristic thresholds (seq_len cutoff, kv_miss tolerance).
eden: Quick note — saw memory spikes during fused path in replay. Uploading artifact: https://artifacts.internal/5604/heapdump.tar.gz
sam: Good call. Also capture timeline traces (KV miss timeline vs kernel invocations) to see if misses cluster at start or are sustained.
eden: I'll attach the timeline once job #5604 completes. For now blocking the staged rollout.
maya: Sound plan. Do we want to add a synthetic variant that simulates KV misses to make synth closer to replay? Might help profiling.
ravi: Yes — add a synthetic workload that injects fake KV miss ratio or random prefix variance, that'll help isolate kernel vs cache.
eden: Thanks — will run the pinned-kernel warmup runs now and follow up with CI outputs. :thumbsup:
